tasks.short: Negotiate supplier and freight terms, secure approval, and record the agreement.

steps.what: Collect spend, volumes, service failures, and current supplier terms.
Compare rate sheets, contract clauses, alternatives, and expected demand.

loop.input: Supplier contracts and quotations, alongside structured spend and demand fields.
loop.output: Cited rate and clause fields for a deterministically calculated negotiation brief.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units, effective dates, and totals; show source passages for every extracted clause.
loop.stop: At most 20 documents and two extraction passes per brief; unresolved fields go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but supplier wording and document layouts vary.

steps.what: Approve target terms, walk-away limits, and escalation boundaries.
Negotiate price, capacity, service commitments, and concessions with the supplier.
Turn agreed deal notes into a contract draft and proposed rate table.

loop.input: Recorded deal notes, approved templates, and the negotiation mandate.
loop.output: Contract draft and proposed rate fields, with deviations highlighted.
loop.check: Match commercial fields to deal notes; flag missing agreement and departures from approved clauses.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved terms remain blank for the procurement specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Template fields are deterministic, but negotiated qualifications arrive in free text.

steps.what: Review legal deviations and reconcile the contract with negotiated commercial terms.
Approve and sign the agreed contract through the signature process.
Enter signed commercial terms and effective dates into purchasing records.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a negotiation brief; bounded extraction adds cited terms from the {CLM}. A bounded drafting step prepares contract paperwork, while people negotiate, review deviations, and sign through the {ESIGN}. After signature, a configured flow publishes the reviewed rate table to the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial evidence was split across transactions, rate sheets, and contracts. Relationships and negotiated exceptions made end-to-end automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and signature workflows handle structured work. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting them, while bounded extraction handles varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier leverage, credible alternatives, capacity promises, and ambiguous concessions require commercial judgement. Contract mapping and access can dominate implementation cost.
tasks.human_edge: Read the supplier's incentives, trade concessions, protect trust, and decide when to walk away.

ambition.what: Structured renewal preparation for smaller suppliers previously receiving only reactive negotiation.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and rewriting agreements, with more time testing alternatives before negotiations. Decision rights do not change automatically; mandates and signing limits still govern commitments.

reach.task: Calculate shipment-level cost-to-serve before freight negotiations.
reach.learn: Tariff structures, shipment characteristics, accessorial charges, and service-cost trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Structured commercial comparisons and publication of approved rates can use deterministic rules.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports rate validation, not negotiation judgement.
A reported Pactum supplier-negotiation case demonstrates automation in a bounded commercial setting; it does not establish suitability for strategic negotiations.

assumptions: Estimates cover one purchasing category and a limited contract-template set.
Use existing reporting and workflow configuration before building connectors.
Supplier communications during negotiation remain human; no autonomous agent is needed.
Apply GDPR controls to supplier contact data and restrict access to confidential commercial records.
unknowns: Available exports, interfaces, and signature-trigger capabilities.
Contract-template quality and the proportion of bespoke clauses.
Delegated negotiation limits, legal-review thresholds, and signing authority.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Which contract fields can be extracted reliably on representative redacted documents?
Can reviewed rate fields be published without rekeying after signature?
Which renewals lack adequate preparation today?
new_work: Review extracted clauses and missing commercial fields.
Resolve discrepancies between deal notes, contract wording, and rate tables.
Maintain templates, field mappings, and signature-trigger rules.

tasks.short: Assess supplier performance and procurement results, then agree improvement priorities.

steps.what: Export purchasing, receipt, quality, and invoice data for the review period.
Join supplier identifiers, reconcile totals, and resolve inconsistent measurement periods.
Calculate supplier scorecards, spend trends, and procurement benefits against agreed baselines.
Investigate performance drivers, baseline distortions, and trade-offs between savings, service, and risk.
Agree supplier-development priorities, accountable owners, and bounded improvement trials.
Publish the review pack and record agreed actions for follow-up.

tasks.design: Configured extracts from the {PROCUREMENT}, {ERP}, and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed deterministic reconciliation and a supplier dashboard in the {BI}. Approved findings populate a templated review pack in the {DOCS} and actions in the {PROJECT}. People interpret causes and approve improvement priorities; no model loop is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier identifiers, metric definitions, and savings baselines differed between teams. Repeated reconciliation was cheaper locally than funding a shared reporting connection.
tasks.enabler_now: Reporting configuration and small reconciliation jobs can replace repeated exports and joins. AI-assisted coding makes those narrow integrations cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: A lower purchase price may conceal poorer service or changed demand. Causal attribution, missing inspection data, and disputed savings baselines remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish genuine supplier improvement from favourable demand, accounting effects, or displaced operational costs.

ambition.what: Weekly supplier-development prioritisation using refreshed cost, quality, and service evidence.

tasks.altitude: The manager reviews exceptions and tests improvement hypotheses instead of rebuilding monthly scorecards. No decision rights change automatically; authority to approve bounded trials would need explicit delegation.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a procurement intervention produced measurable operational benefits.
reach.learn: Baseline design, mix adjustment, causal limitations, and benefit measurement.

evidence.claim: Supplier scorecards, reconciliation checks, and templated reporting can use deterministic calculations.
Automated scorecards do not establish causality or remove the need to judge procurement trade-offs.
Transporeon provides agreed-rate freight invoice checks, an adjacent source of cost-control evidence rather than a full supplier-effectiveness assessment.

assumptions: Estimates cover a limited metric set, one business unit, and batch refreshes.
Aggregate supplier measures are the target; individual employee scoring is outside scope.
The high automation prior fits data preparation better than causal interpretation or action selection.
Access design applies GDPR where contact or other personal data enters the dataset.
unknowns: Supplier identifier consistency and available historical data.
Agreed definitions of on-time delivery, quality failure, and realised savings.
Whether relevant reporting is already configured.
Data ownership, access approval times, and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can one review period be reconciled to financial and operational control totals?
Which scorecard measures change decisions rather than merely describe activity?
How much analyst effort comes from recurring data defects?
new_work: Resolve unmatched suppliers and failed reconciliation checks.
Version metric definitions and procurement baselines.
Check whether improvement trials produce sustained benefits.

tasks.short: Track supplier delivery and quality exceptions and coordinate corrective action.

steps.what: Review open orders, promised dates, receipts, and overdue deliveries.
Check inspection outcomes against agreed quality limits and validate unusual flags.
Combine delivery and quality exceptions and identify affected orders and production needs.
Request missing delivery dates, evidence, or explanations from the supplier.
Read supplier replies and record claimed causes, recovery dates, and supporting evidence.

loop.input: Replies and attachments linked to a specific supplier exception.
loop.output: Attributed supplier claims, proposed recovery dates, and evidence references.
loop.check: Require order references and quoted evidence; distinguish supplier claims from verified facts.
loop.stop: One thread, up to ten attachments, and two extraction passes; ambiguity goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Suppliers describe causes and conditional dates in varied free text.

steps.what: Discuss recovery options with suppliers and internal operational owners.
Approve delegated containment actions and log owners, deadlines, and required escalations.

tasks.design: Configured exception views in the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed a joined supplier register on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A configured flow sends standard evidence requests through the {EMAIL}, and a bounded loop extracts attributed claims for review. People agree recovery actions, while the {PROJECT} tracks approved owners and deadlines.
tasks.previous_blocker: Receipt events, inspection outcomes, and supplier replies were disconnected. Managers supplied the missing links through spreadsheets and mailbox follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing date and quality rules can generate exceptions. Small integrations connect affected orders, while bounded extraction reduces reply handling without deciding supplier credibility.
tasks.still_hard: Missing events, revised promises, partial deliveries, and disputed responsibility create false alarms. Physical recovery, quality release, and credible supplier commitments remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a recovery promise is credible and balance continuity, quality, cost, and supplier relationships.

ambition.what: An early supplier-risk briefing for production planners before threatened material shortages.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on threatened production and recovery choices, with fewer routine status chases. Decision rights do not change automatically; quality release and spending approvals retain their designated approvers.

reach.task: Prioritise material shortages against the production schedule.
reach.learn: Material dependencies, usable stock, production cut-offs, and recovery lead times.

reach.task: Define evidence needed to resolve supplier quality exceptions.
reach.learn: Inspection limits, traceability, containment, and release authority.

evidence.claim: Order-date rules, quality thresholds, and event joins can identify supplier exceptions deterministically.
A bounded extraction step can structure supplier replies while preserving attribution and human verification.
A supplier's stated recovery date is evidence to assess, not proof that delivery will occur.

assumptions: Estimates cover one operational site and a limited supplier cohort.
Automatic external requests use approved factual templates and cannot make concessions or commitments.
Flag generation does not release stock, approve substitutions, or place expedite orders.
GDPR controls cover supplier contacts; employee monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Where inspection records and supplier confirmations are held.
Reliability and latency of receipt, inspection, and promised-date events.
Permitted supplier contact channels and existing notification rules.
Delegated containment limits and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which exceptions predict operational disruption early enough to change the outcome?
How often do missing receipts or revised promises create false alarms?
Can supplier replies be matched to orders without ambiguous references?
new_work: Review ambiguous supplier claims and unmatched replies.
Correct missing operational events and stale promised dates.
Tune thresholds and suppress duplicate requests.
Maintain contact records, access controls, and escalation paths.

tasks.short: Design and implement supply-chain changes that balance strategy, cost, service, and resilience.

steps.what: Collect demand, stock, capacity, supplier, transport, and cost data for the current network.
Define strategic objectives, service promises, constraints, and acceptable transition risks.
Model alternative sourcing, inventory, warehouse, and transport designs.
Write the recommendation, assumptions, sensitivities, and proposed transition approach.

loop.input: Validated scenario tables, recorded assumptions, and the manager's selected recommendation.
loop.output: A cited business-case draft with sensitivities, unresolved questions, and transition risks.
loop.check: Insert figures directly from validated tables; link claims to inputs and reject unsupported benefits.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per business case; unresolved claims become explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Figures use templates, but the strategic rationale and caveats require free-text synthesis.

steps.what: Select the design and approve investment, risk limits, and pilot scope.
Create delivery workstreams, owners, milestones, and approval checkpoints.
Coordinate the pilot, resolve operational constraints, and support affected teams.
Compare pilot cost, service, capacity, and reliability against the approved baseline.
Approve wider rollout, require redesign, or stop the change.

tasks.design: A governed baseline on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {CRM}, with deterministic scenario calculations presented in the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts the selected business case in the {DOCS}, and configured templates create an approved implementation plan in the {PROJECT}. People set objectives, approve investment, lead the pilot, and decide rollout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Network models were expensive to assemble and became stale between projects. Strategic constraints, uncertain demand, and physical implementation prevented a simple automated decision process.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings and deterministic scenario calculations reduce repeat modelling work. AI-assisted coding helps build a narrower planning tool without requiring a new forecasting breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Results depend on demand assumptions, real capacity, supplier behaviour, and transition disruption. Physical network changes, workforce implications, and consultation can take far longer than the software build.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which strategic trade-offs matter, challenge model assumptions, and secure cooperation during operational change.

ambition.what: Quarterly network resilience reviews of alternate sourcing and stock-location options.

tasks.altitude: The manager can refresh scenarios between major redesign projects and spend more time shaping options with operational teams. Investment and rollout rights remain with existing approvers; any delegated pilot budget needs explicit agreement.

reach.task: Test supply disruption scenarios and recovery options.
reach.learn: Recovery objectives, critical dependencies, scenario severity, and practical fallback capacity.

reach.task: Translate an approved network design into a staged operational rollout.
reach.learn: Dependency planning, readiness criteria, change control, and benefits tracking.

evidence.claim: Slim4 provides inventory forecasting and stock-setting capabilities; this supports a component of supply-chain design.
ORTEC provides route-planning capabilities; route optimisation does not settle wider strategic network choices.
A Slim4 vendor case reports stock falling over 20% with availability above 98%; the period is unstated and results are not transferable guarantees.
Deterministic cost-to-serve and constraint scenarios can support managerial decisions without an autonomous agent.

assumptions: Estimates cover decision-support software for a bounded network, not physical relocation or full operational rollout.
Reuse existing planning configuration where it covers the scenario before adding custom calculations.
Scenario outputs are conditional estimates; they do not establish future demand or supplier capacity.
Access and consultation estimates allow initial review; national rules may require longer employee or works-council consultation.
Use aggregate operational data where possible and apply GDPR controls to personal data.
unknowns: Network size, model scope, and availability of reliable cost and capacity data.
Capabilities and licences of existing planning systems.
Investment authority, pilot budgets, and operational readiness requirements.
Workforce effects, applicable national consultation rules, and required lead times.
Supplier commitments and contractual constraints on proposed changes.
research_questions: Can the baseline reproduce observed cost and service within agreed tolerances?
Which decisions remain stable when demand, lead time, and capacity assumptions change?
What is the smallest reversible pilot that tests the proposed design?
Which implementation constraints are missing from the numerical model?
new_work: Maintain cost, capacity, lead-time, and constraint assumptions.
Review scenario feasibility and sensitivity to uncertain inputs.
Check generated business cases against validated results.
Track pilot readiness, consultation outcomes, and realised benefits.
Maintain data mappings and model versions.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward commercial judgement, supplier recovery, and repeated testing of supply-chain options. Preparation and reporting shrink, while negotiation, operational leadership, and investment approvals remain human responsibilities.
reach: Logistics Analysts: connect shipment economics to supplier and network decisions.
Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks: link supplier exceptions to material shortages and production priorities.
Business Continuity Planners: test disruption recovery options against real capacity.
Project Management Specialists: turn approved designs into staged, measurable changes.
skills_to_grow: Define consistent supplier, service, and cost measures.
Validate data joins and challenge misleading baselines.
Interpret scenario sensitivities and operational constraints.
Design reversible pilots and measure realised benefits.
Review cited model outputs and maintain appropriate access.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring supply-chain decision service: refresh supplier risks, prepare commercial alternatives, and test resilience options before disruption forces a decision. Seek explicit delegation for bounded improvement pilots, supported by measured results.
